subject: MedQuery model fit intake: sample harvest + redaction check
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@medquery.ai>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@medquery.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: MedQuery model fit intake: sample harvest + redaction check

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation and very helpful context. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs
- Use case: conversational triage + candidate summarization for clinical research queries (non-diagnostic).
- Expected traffic: ~3 M tokens/day initially, 95th pct latency SLO ~350ms per token for short interactions.
- Data sensitivity: mix of de-identified examples + a handful of free-text clinical notes (possible PHI).
- Success criteria: precision on entity extraction > 92% for key fields; no leakage of raw PHI in outputs.

Model / eval guidance (initial recommendations)
- For an eval we recommend starting with two variants: a high-quality base (redwood-chat-amber medium-sized instruct) and a quantized throughput profile (redwood-large-quant-v1) for token-cost comparisons. Benchmarks we referenced are here: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/medquery-2026 (public to you with this link).
- We'll run both generation and extraction tasks: end-to-end prompts you provide + a measured set of edge cases (see below).

What we need from you (action items)
1) Prompt harvest: a CSV with representative user prompts (200–500 rows recommended). Columns we find helpful: prompt_text, intent_label, expected_output_snippet, sensitivity_flag (yes/no), source_example_id.
2) Edge case set: 15–30 tricky prompts where you see frequent failures (ambiguity, redaction failures, hallucination-prone queries).
3) Redaction guidance: a short doc calling out fields you consider PHI and any company-specific redaction rules. If anything must never be surfaced (e.g., patient identifiers), call it out explicitly.

Security & compliance note
- Our private/Dedicated options include VPC connectors and KMS integration. For anything with PHI we recommend Redwood Private; if you want, I’ll loop our security lead to do a brief review of your DOCS and retention policy.

Proposed timeline
- File delivery (your side): by Tue 7/14 ideally.
- Redwood: initial eval run within 5 business days of file receipt; share bench + quality recap and recommended quant/config options.

Attachments referenced: example CSV template (attached) and a short redaction checklist template.

Next step: Emily — can you confirm whether you can share a 200–500 prompt sample and the redaction doc by 7/14? Also flag any internal security contacts we should work with.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MedQuery model fit intake: sample harvest + redaction check

Thanks Jordan — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick answers and an initial upload attached.

What I attached
- mediquery_prompt_samples.csv (contains ~260 user prompts taken from our support logs and research pilots).
- mediquery_redaction_examples.docx (examples of fields we consider PHI and a few redaction rules we use).

Notes / constraints
- A subset (~12) of the prompts include verbatim patient mentions; those are flagged in the CSV with sensitivity_flag = yes. We’d prefer those be handled in a private/Dedicated environment.
- We also have a compliance checklist — Alex (cc) will share our SOC export if you need it.

Questions for Redwood team
1) For the quantized profile you suggested, how do you handle KV cache persistence between requests? We prefer short-lived caches but want to avoid cold-token cost for multi-turn sessions.
2) Can you confirm whether any prompt-level PII is stored by default in hosted mode? We need explicit retention windows.

I quoted your note below for context.

Subject: Re: MedQuery model fit intake: sample harvest + redaction check

Emily — thanks for the files, received and ingested into the eval pipeline. A couple quick clarifications and what you should expect next: 

Clarifications
- CSV looks great — we validated columns and randomized a 50-row sample for sensitive content. The flagged rows are handled in a private sandbox for the run and won’t touch hosted logs.
- KV cache: for the quantized throughput profile we use short-lived KV caches (~30s TTL) by default with an option to pin for session-based workloads. I’ve noted your preference for short-lived caches and will default to 30s for the evaluation run.
- Retention: in hosted mode default retention is 30 days for logs/metrics; prompt payloads are not stored beyond that unless you enable longer retention. For PHI we recommend Private (customers keep control).

Initial model plan and links
- Run set: redwood-chat-amber (instruction-tuned medium) + redwood-large-quant-v1 (intended for throughput/cost tradeoffs).
- We’ll produce per-prompt precision/recall and a hallucination score for the sample set. Bench URL again: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/medquery-2026.

Deliverables & timeline
- Initial bench + quality recap: EOD Thu 7/16.
- Follow-up sync (30m): Fri 7/17 — propose 10:00 AM PT. Marissa — are you available to join?

If anything else comes up (additional edge cases or special redaction rules), drop them into the shared Drive link and we’ll pick them up before the run.

Best,
Jordan
